question_text: What was Job's character described as in the land of Uz?

options.a: Blameless and upright, fearing God and turning away from evil
options.b: A proud king over many nations
options.c: A priest serving in the temple
options.d: A warrior who defeated many enemies

question_text: What advice did Job's wife give him during his suffering?

options.a: Pray to God for healing
options.b: Curse God and die
options.c: Offer a sacrifice to the LORD
options.d: Leave the country

question_text: What did Job do when he finally broke his silence?

options.a: He asked God for wealth
options.b: He rebuked his three friends
options.c: He cursed the day of his birth
options.d: He sang a song of victory

question_text: Who was the first of Job's three friends to speak to him?

options.a: Eliphaz the Temanite
options.b: Bildad the Shuhite
options.c: Zophar the Naamathite
options.d: Elihu the Buzite

question_text: What did Eliphaz advise Job to do regarding God's correction?

options.a: Reject God's authority
options.b: Do not despise the discipline of the Almighty
options.c: Flee to another land
options.d: Refuse to listen to any counsel

question_text: How did Job describe his grief and suffering in response to Eliphaz?

options.a: A temporary misunderstanding
options.b: Easy to endure with patience
options.c: Heavier than the sand of the seas
options.d: Lighter than a feather

question_text: What does Job compare human life to in his complaint?

options.a: A mighty fortress
options.b: An unshakeable mountain
options.c: A deep and everlasting river
options.d: A breath or a wind that passes away

question_text: What argument did Bildad the Shuhite bring forward to Job?

options.a: God is unjust and ignores human misery
options.b: God does not pervert justice, so Job's children must have sinned
options.c: Job should become a king to solve his problems
options.d: Job's wealth will return tomorrow

question_text: What fundamental problem does Job express regarding arguing with God?

options.a: Angels will prevent man from speaking
options.b: God is too far away to listen to anyone
options.c: How can a mortal man be right before God?
options.d: Human speech is forbidden before God

question_text: What does Job ask God in his prayer of despair?

options.a: Where are my army commanders?
options.b: Why did You make me a ruler?
options.c: When will You build me a palace?
options.d: Why did You bring me out of the womb?

question_text: What did Zophar the Naamathite accuse Job of being?

options.a: A man full of talk who justifies himself
options.b: A silent coward
options.c: An enemy of Egypt
options.d: A traitor to his tribe

question_text: How did Job sarcastically reply to his three friends?

options.a: I agree with every word you have spoken!
options.b: You are the greatest prophets of God!
options.c: Doubtless you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!
options.d: Please teach me all of your knowledge!

question_text: What confident statement does Job make about his trust in God despite his pain?

options.a: I will seek help from false idols
options.b: I will curse God until I die
options.c: I will rely on my own righteousness
options.d: Though He slay me, yet will I hope in Him

question_text: What does Job say about a person born of woman?

options.a: He is few of days and full of trouble
options.b: He lives forever on the earth
options.c: He is always free from sorrow
options.d: He has divine power

question_text: What did Eliphaz claim Job's own words were doing?

options.a: Bringing revival to the nation
options.b: Condemning him and undermining piety
options.c: Pleasing the angels
options.d: Proving his total innocence

question_text: What famous title did Job give to his three friends in response?

options.a: Faithful servants of God
options.b: True brothers in Christ
options.c: Wise advisors of the East
options.d: Miserable comforters are you all

question_text: Where does Job say his hope is going down to?

options.a: The gates of death / dust
options.b: The palace of the king
options.c: The highest heaven
options.d: The rich lands of Canaan

question_text: What theme does Bildad focus on in his second speech?

options.a: The forgiveness and grace of God
options.b: The terrible fate and darkness of the wicked
options.c: The creation of the heavens
options.d: The blessing of large families

question_text: What famous declaration of faith does Job make in chapter 19?

options.a: I know that my wealth will be doubled immediately
options.b: I know that I will conquer all my enemies tomorrow
options.c: I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last He will stand upon the earth
options.d: I know that my friends are telling the truth

question_text: What does Zophar claim about the triumph of the wicked?

options.a: It lasts for generations without end
options.b: It is short, and the joy of the godless is brief
options.c: It is blessed by God
options.d: It leads to eternal peace

question_text: What observation does Job make that counters his friends' claims?

options.a: The righteous never suffer under any circumstances
options.b: The wicked are always punished immediately in this life
options.c: The wicked often live on, grow old, and increase in power
options.d: God gives all material riches only to the holy

question_text: What specific false sins does Eliphaz accuse Job of committing?

options.a: Worshipping the sun and moon openly
options.b: Leading an army to burn down cities
options.c: Stealing golden idols from temples
options.d: Stripping clothing from the naked and withholding water from the weary

question_text: What does Job express a deep longing to do in chapter 23?

options.a: To flee into the desert and hide forever
options.b: To find God and present his case before His seat
options.c: To fight his comforters with weapons
options.d: To return to his youth and start over

question_text: What question does Job ask regarding God's judgment on injustice?

options.a: Why do the poor oppress the rich?
options.b: Why does God destroy the righteous and save no one?
options.c: Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment?
options.d: Why is there no sun in the sky?

question_text: What is Bildad's main point in his short final speech?

options.a: The stars are brighter than God
options.b: Job should offer 100 bulls as a sacrifice
options.c: God needs human wisdom to govern
options.d: How can a man be righteous before God, who is so majestic?

question_text: How does Job describe God's power over creation?

options.a: He built the world inside a giant temple
options.b: He relies on angels to hold up the pillars of earth
options.c: He hangs the earth on nothing and spreads out the northern skies
options.d: He rests without paying attention to the seas

question_text: What vow does Job make regarding his integrity?

options.a: I will give up my belief in God's justice
options.b: I will admit to crimes I did not commit to stop the pain
options.c: I will follow the advice of Zophar and Bildad
options.d: As long as I have breath, my lips will not speak wickedness

question_text: What is the central theme and conclusion of Job's poem in chapter 28?

options.a: The fear of the Lord—that is wisdom, and to shun evil is understanding
options.b: Wisdom is found by digging deep into gold mines
options.c: Wisdom can be purchased with vast amounts of silver
options.d: Only kings and rulers possess true wisdom

question_text: What does Job reflect on in chapter 29?

options.a: The past days when God watched over him and he was respected
options.b: His plan to build a larger household
options.c: His childhood in the land of Canaan
options.d: His desire to travel across the sea

question_text: How does Job describe his current reality compared to his past status?

options.a: Even young men whose fathers he disdained now mock him
options.b: He is treated like a king by the whole city
options.c: He has been given a seat of honor at the gate
options.d: His neighbors bring him gifts every day

question_text: What covenant did Job say he made with his eyes?

options.a: Not to look at the sun at noon
options.b: Not to look lustfully at a young woman
options.c: Not to sleep during the day
options.d: Not to gaze upon gold or silver

question_text: Why had Elihu waited until now to speak?

options.a: Because God commanded him to stay silent until day seven
options.b: Because he was afraid of Job
options.c: Because he had just arrived from a distant country
options.d: Because the others were older than he

question_text: What means does Elihu say God uses to speak to people and turn them from pit?

options.a: Through dreams, visions, and pain/chastisement
options.b: Through military victories and wealth
options.c: Through human laws and taxation
options.d: God never speaks to humans directly or indirectly

question_text: What attribute of God does Elihu emphasize in chapter 34?

options.a: God favors the rich over the poor
options.b: God will never do wickedly, nor will the Almighty pervert justice
options.c: God changes His mind based on human complaints
options.d: God acts without any moral standards

question_text: According to Elihu, why do people cry out when oppressed without receiving an answer?

options.a: Because God cannot hear human voices
options.b: Because God is too busy running the universe
options.c: Because they cry out in pride without seeking God their Maker
options.d: Because angels block their prayers

question_text: How does Elihu describe God's handling of the righteous and the afflicted?

options.a: He does not take His eyes off the righteous and delivers the afflicted through suffering
options.b: He ignores the righteous and exalts only the wicked
options.c: He treats everyone with equal harshness
options.d: He leaves human destiny entirely to luck

question_text: What natural phenomena does Elihu point to as evidence of God's majestic power?

options.a: Volcanoes and earthquakes only
options.b: Thunder, lightning, snow, and torrential rain
options.c: The movement of ocean tides only
options.d: Solar eclipses only

question_text: How does the LORD answer Job out of the whirlwind?

options.a: I have come to give you back your children immediately.
options.b: You are correct Job, and your friends are wrong about everything.
options.c: Who is this that obscures my plans with words without knowledge?
options.d: Listen to the wisdom of Elihu and follow his law.

question_text: Which creatures does God highlight to show His sovereign care and design?

options.a: The fish of the ocean and corals
options.b: The dragon, serpent, and leviathan only
options.c: The domestic sheep, cow, and goat only
options.d: The mountain goat, wild donkey, ostrich, horse, and eagle

question_text: What mighty creature does God describe to Job in chapter 40?

options.a: The Great Sphinx
options.b: Behemoth, which ranks first among the works of God
options.c: The Phoenix
options.d: The Golden Eagle

question_text: What sea creature is described in detail to illustrate God's unstoppable power?

options.a: The Kraken
options.b: The Great Whale
options.c: Leviathan
options.d: The Hydra

question_text: What was Job's final response to God, and how did God bless him afterward?

options.a: Job left his land to start a new nation
options.b: Job argued back, and God punished him further
options.c: Job remained silent, and his friends became rulers
options.d: Job repented in dust and ashes, and God restored twice as much as he had before
